item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
How does this not have a million upvotes.

As sure as a billy goat's prone to act goatly

This is the best line.

There are one or two spots that I would tweak ("of all of existence - scenario XK!"), and I would really love it if you changed "not one single use!" to something that rhymed with "black box", because I can't honestly figure out how to parse that line and you did so well with the expungement and redactions. But this is just fantastic, regardless. :D

Yeah, +1. This is still cute. I don't mind that the rhyme scheme dances around a bit (Seuss didn't mind that himself, honestly), and I think you did a decent job on it. If you get time, polish it up a little more and try to get your syllables more in line with a more natural patter.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Echoing this. This tale falls flat and is somewhat uninteresting because it certainly sounds like Dr. Seuss, but doesn't feel like Dr. Seuss. It's not so whimsical, or compelling, or in the spirit of his characters; it just sounds somewhat like an object written up in his style, which alone isn't interesting. I would fully support this provided that was dealt with.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Scince it's written up this way, I'm forced to react to this as a tale-form SCP. The result?

Beyond the flowery, purple prose, this is a simple Thing What Kills You, which makes you speak in bad poetry if ypu spend too much time near it. The format screw makes it near-worthless as any sort of scientific document- what's the audible range of the SCP, for instance?

Knowing that it's a crossover with Sweeny Todd doesn't improve the article in my mind, since it wholly relies on the rhyming to be good.
